addressedFindings.summary: The Tier-A publisher bound asOf to the run wall-clock, a field the contract defines as the analyzed window, so any run not beginning exactly on its window boundary published an artifact its own consumer had to refuse.
addressedFindings.resolution: scripts/brief-refresh.mjs now sets asOf from RLPORTFOLIOBRIEF.windowCutoffAt(cfg.windows, window, snap.ts) and throws when a window has no resolvable cutoff. generatedAt keeps the run instant, so the two clocks are genuinely distinct on the published artifacts.

addressedFindings.summary: The cutoff rule existed in two places that could drift: the consumer derived it from the declared schedule, and any publisher deriving it independently would agree only until the schedule changed.
addressedFindings.resolution: windowCutoffAt() is defined once in rlportfoliobrief.js and exported. The publisher, the payload validator and the consumer all call it, and the declared ET times are never restated as literals.

addressedFindings.summary: A refused evidence window emptied the schedule selector, because the schedule and the evidence window shared one load transaction. A control with zero options tells the reader 'there is nothing here', which is false.
addressedFindings.resolution: portfolio-survival-allocation-lab.html renders the selector from the public schedule before composition is attempted, and the .catch() names the contract code and reason via data-generic-window-error and in reader-visible copy.

addressedFindings.summary: The cockpit read the publication clock from payloadRef.asOf. That was silently correct only because the publisher stamped both fields identically, and became wrong the moment the publisher fix made them differ.
addressedFindings.resolution: The publication clock reads snapshotRef.generatedAt at portfolio-survival-allocation-lab.html:8110. This is the characteristic hazard of un-collapsing two wrongly-equal fields: every consumer that read either one was correct by accident, and the fix converts each into a real choice.

addressedFindings.summary: scripts/brief-narrative-parallel.mjs fell back from snapshot.asOf to snapshot.generatedAt and then to a fresh wall-clock, either of which would republish the defect under a different name.
addressedFindings.resolution: The fallback chain is replaced by an explicit throw. Absence fails loudly rather than being papered over with a run clock.

addressedFindings.summary: notes/market-brief.md documented the defect as intended behaviour, stating that Tier-A sets both fields to the run time.
addressedFindings.resolution: The sentence now states the implemented rule. The definition in the preceding sentences was already correct and is unchanged.

openDiscoveries.summary: Whether a persistently late publication should surface HOW late it was, rather than only being made honest about its two clocks.
openDiscoveries.why: The fix makes an 11:37 publication of the 11:00 window honest: it declares 11:00 evidence and discloses an 11:37 publication instant. It does not surface lateness as an operational signal, and a brief published hours after its cutoff is well-formed but practically stale. Adding a staleness disclosure in the same change that first makes the two clocks differ would leave no run in which to observe whether the distinction alone is sufficient.
